newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court drops bid to block Tyumen Oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian court drops bid to block Tyumen Oil sale.

text.p: The arbitration court of Russia's Tyumen region cancelled a decision last week calling for the forthcoming investment tender of 40 percent of the Tyumen Oil Company (TNK) to be cancelled, a court official said Monday.
Viktor Vitoshkin, deputy chairman of the court in the Siberian city of Tyumen where TNK is based, said the decision to drop the appeal on Sunday was based on a request from TNK.
"We took this decision (to drop the appeal), because yesterday a petition was made to us by Tyumen Oil Company itself to the effect that it wanted to be sold," Vitoshkin told Reuters.
"Because the earlier decision was based on an appeal made by one of TNK's shareholders, the petition from TNK has nullified the reason for the investment tender to be cancelled."

TNK President Alexander Furman represented those arguing for dropping the blockade on the sale at a court meeting and Viktor Pali, general director of Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS, those arguing against dropping it, a TNK source said.

Nizhnevartovskneftegaz is TNK's main production unit. TNK's 1996 production, which accounted for about seven percent of Russia's total oil output that year, fell six percent to 426,000 barrels per day.
Russia's powerful consortium Alfa-Group, combining Alfa-Bank, Alfa-EKO, Alfa-Kapital and Alfa-Estate, is one of at least six bidders in the TNK tender, a company spokesman said.
The TNK investment tender, one of the last sell-offs of a major Russian oil company, has come under fire in recent weeks as company officials argue over terms and desirability of the sale.

A 40 percent stake carries a price tag of around $25 million and $160 million in investment over two years. Russia is also due to offer around 47 percent of TNK through special cash auctions starting August 5.
